extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of American political history (general public, scholars interested in 19th‑century New York politics)
extracted.subtask_description: A chapter-length historical narrative describing the rise, organization, and corrupt practices of Tammany Hall and its leaders in 19th-century New York City. Focuses on political machines, patronage, municipal government changes, and examples of financial corruption under Tweed and his allies.
